cards.explanation: The answer is to take a census of Israel. The text says Satan "…incited David to take a census of Israel." (1 Chronicles 21:1). David is Israel's king, and the push to start counting comes from Satan. A headcount sounds harmless, friends, but this one is where the trouble starts.

The answer is that Joab asks why David would bring guilt on Israel. Joab, David's army commander (1 Chronicles 27:34), asks, "Why should he bring guilt on Israel?" (1 Chronicles 21:3). He's the guy in the meeting who says "Are we SURE about this?" while everybody else is already picking up their pens. He even asks, "…are they not all servants of my lord?"

The answer is False. Joab pushes back, but "…the king’s word prevailed against Joab." (1 Chronicles 21:4). David doesn't call anything off, friends. Joab, David's army commander (1 Chronicles 27:34), travels through Israel and then returns to Jerusalem.

The answer is Levi. The text says Joab "…did not include Levi and Benjamin in the count…" (1 Chronicles 21:6). Two tribes get skipped. The same verse gives the reason: the king's command was detestable to Joab.

The answer is True. Joab, David's army commander (1 Chronicles 27:34), leaves out Levi and Benjamin "…because the king’s command was detestable to him." (1 Chronicles 21:6). He carries out the order, but he's clearly not at peace with it. Joab argued against it from the start (1 Chronicles 21:3).

The answer is False. No blame goes to Joab. David says to God, "I have sinned greatly because I have done this thing." (1 Chronicles 21:8). He takes it on himself and says he "…acted very foolishly." There's no pointing a finger anywhere else, friends.

The answer is three options to choose from. The LORD instructs Gad, David's seer, to go and tell David, and the message is, "I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you." (1 Chronicles 21:10). David has to pick one. The three are three years of famine, three months of being swept away before his enemies, or three days of the sword of the LORD (1 Chronicles 21:12).

The answer is that David chooses to fall into the hand of the LORD. He says, "Please, let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men." (1 Chronicles 21:13). He also says he's deeply distressed, and I think that's an honest thing to say.

The answer is mercies. David says, "…for His mercies are very great…" (1 Chronicles 21:13). He's in a tight spot with three hard options, friends, and what he leans on is the LORD's mercy. I think that says a lot about what he knows of God.

The answer is False. The LORD saw it, "…relented from the calamity…" and said to the angel, "Enough! Withdraw your hand now!" (1 Chronicles 21:15). The angel doesn't get to keep going. The LORD stops him.

The answer is that they fall facedown, clothed in sackcloth. David and the elders, "…clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown." (1 Chronicles 21:16). The elders are Israel's leaders, and they go down on their faces together. This is a heavy moment, friends.

The answer is True. David says, "O LORD my God, please let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house, but do not let this plague remain upon Your people." (1 Chronicles 21:17). He asks for it to land on himself and his family instead. I think that's a shepherd's heart, since he calls them "these sheep."

The answer is Ornan. The angel of the LORD orders Gad, David's seer, to tell David to build an altar "…on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite." (1 Chronicles 21:18). A threshing floor is where grain gets separated from the husks. David goes up at the word Gad spoke in the name of the LORD (1 Chronicles 21:19).

The answer is that they hide themselves. Ornan sees the angel, and "…his four sons who were with him hid themselves." (1 Chronicles 21:20). Ornan is the one working the threshing floor. I think they were scared stiff, friends, but that part is just my guess.

The answer is that Ornan offers to give David all of it. Ornan says, "Take it! May my lord the king do whatever seems good to him." (1 Chronicles 21:23). Then he offers the oxen, the sledges and the wheat, saying, "…I will give it all." David won't take it for free, though, and says he insists on paying the full price (1 Chronicles 21:24).

The answer is that David won't give offerings that cost him nothing. He says, "…I will not take for the LORD what belongs to you, nor will I offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing." (1 Chronicles 21:24). Ornan's gift is generous, friends, but David wants the offering to be his own. So he pays.

The answer is fire. David "…called upon the LORD, who answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering." (1 Chronicles 21:26). He paid full price, built the altar, and the LORD answered right there.
The answer is True. "Then the LORD spoke to the angel, who put his sword back into its sheath." (1 Chronicles 21:27). The angel who had a drawn sword over Jerusalem puts it away, friends.

The answer is that David says, here will be the house of the LORD God. He says, "Here shall be the house of the LORD God, as well as the altar of burnt offering for Israel." (1 Chronicles 22:1). He picks out Ornan's threshing floor, the place where he built an altar to the LORD.
